title: Jets QB Geno Smith Escapes Major Ankle Injury, Tests Reveal No Serious Damage – ESPN Report
body:
New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith escaped a potentially season‑altering ankle injury after a series of imaging tests on Monday revealed no serious damage to his left foot. The findings, confirmed by team physicians and relayed to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, mean the veteran signal‑caller can return to full practice without the lingering doubt of a fracture or ligament tear that could have sidelined him for weeks.

Smith’s injury occurred during the Jets’ week‑three matchup against the New England Patriots, when he slipped on a wet field and twisted his left ankle while attempting to evade a sack. He was briefly helped off the field but remained in the game, completing 18 of 28 passes for 207 yards and a touchdown. The incident sparked immediate concern among fans and analysts, who feared a high‑ankle sprain or even a broken fibula, injuries that have plagued quarterbacks in recent seasons and often require extensive rehabilitation.

Following the game, the Jets’ medical staff ordered X‑rays and an MRI to assess the extent of the trauma. The scans showed only mild soft‑tissue swelling and no fracture lines, dislocations, or significant ligament disruption. “We’re relieved to see there’s no major structural injury,” a Jets spokesperson said, adding that Smith will continue with a conservative treatment plan that includes rest, ice, compression and a brief course of anti‑inflammatory medication. The team expects the quarterback to resume full‑speed drills within the next few days, with a tentative return to the sidelines slated for the upcoming Thursday night contest against the Buffalo Bills.

Smith’s health is a critical factor for New York, which entered the season with a roster that blends emerging talent and seasoned veterans. After a shaky start that left the Jets 1‑2, the offense has leaned heavily on Smith’s experience and poise under pressure. His ability to manage the game, limit turnovers and execute the play‑action concepts designed by offensive coordinator Nathaniel Hackett has been instrumental in keeping the team competitive. A prolonged absence could have forced the Jets to rely on backup quarterback Zach Wilson, whose limited preseason action has left questions about his readiness for a full‑time role.

The broader NFL landscape also underscores the significance of Smith’s quick clearance. Quarterbacks across the league have faced a spate of lower‑body injuries that have reshaped playoff pictures, from Aaron Rodgers’ calf strain to Josh Allen’s ankle sprain. Teams with depth at the quarterback position have been better positioned to absorb such blows, while those lacking a reliable backup have seen their postseason hopes waver. For the Jets, maintaining continuity at the most pivotal position is essential as they navigate a demanding schedule that includes road games in hostile environments and a divisional showdown with the Miami Dolphins.

Looking ahead, the Jets will monitor Smith’s ankle closely, employing a gradual increase in workload to avoid any setbacks. If the quarterback remains injury‑free, he is poised to guide New York through a critical stretch of games that could determine whether the team secures a wild‑card berth or falls short of postseason contention. The next few weeks will test both Smith’s resilience and the coaching staff’s ability to adapt the offensive scheme to his strengths, setting the tone for the Jets’ aspirations as the season progresses.
